title: Rotate the vCenter session secret without stranding in-flight requests
prompt:
Implement `vcenter/client.go` as a standard-library-only Go client for the vSphere Automation API for vCenter in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0. Do not add dependencies or edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection derived directly from `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable commit `85151f6b1bb58f13b6ac0304bfec53904bea085f`, the 9.0.0.0 revision of that file. Its provenance is repeated in `docs/official_sources.json`, including the spec path and a separate pinned source record for every operationId. No rendered documentation page and no later revision of the same specification is a contract source. Use exactly the specification operationIds `Cis.Session_create`, `Cis.Session_delete`, and `Vcenter.VM_list`; do not call another route. The document's only server is `https://{host}/api`, so every request target is the service root followed by `/api` and the operation path.

Preserve the supplied public API and types: `NewClient(serviceRoot string, credential Credential, httpClient *http.Client) (*Client, error)`, `(*Client).Login(ctx context.Context) error`, `(*Client).ListVMs(ctx context.Context, filter Filter) ([]VM, error)`, `(*Client).Rotate(ctx context.Context, next Credential) error`, `(*Client).Logout(ctx context.Context) error`, `Credential`, `Filter`, `VM`, `APIError`, `ProtocolError`, `ErrNoSession`, and `ErrSessionActive`. A nil HTTP client means `http.DefaultClient`. Reject a service root that is not an absolute `http` or `https` URL or that carries a path, query, fragment, or userinfo, and reject a blank username or password wherever a credential is supplied. Reject a nil context. `Login` on a client that already holds a live session returns `ErrSessionActive`; `ListVMs`, `Rotate`, and `Logout` without a live session return `ErrNoSession` and send nothing. Never expose a password or a session token in an error or a result.

`Login` calls `Cis.Session_create` with the current credential and keeps the returned token. `Rotate` performs a credential rotation that must not strand requests already on the wire: create the replacement session with `next` first, make its token the one every request started from then on uses, wait until every request that had already acquired the previous token has finished, and only then call `Cis.Session_delete` for the previous token. A failed replacement `Cis.Session_create` leaves the previous session current and undeleted. A failed `Cis.Session_delete` is reported once, with no retry, after the replacement token is already current. `Logout` drains the current session the same way before deleting it. The client is used concurrently: `ListVMs` calls running in other goroutines must never be issued with, or answered on, a token that has already been deleted, and a rotation must not lock them out. `go test -race ./...` is the bar.

Honor the exact wire contract. All three operations are bodyless: no request body, no `Content-Type`, no transfer encoding, and no positive content length. Every request carries exactly one `Accept: application/json`. `Cis.Session_create` is `POST /api/session` carrying exactly one basic_auth `Authorization` header built from the credential and no `vmware-api-session-id`; it requires exactly HTTP 201 with JSON media type and a bare, nonblank, header-safe JSON string body, so an object such as a `value` wrapper is not a session token. `Cis.Session_delete` is `DELETE /api/session` carrying exactly one `vmware-api-session-id` header and no `Authorization`, and requires exactly HTTP 204. `Vcenter.VM_list` is `GET /api/vcenter/vm` carrying exactly one `vmware-api-session-id` header and no `Authorization`.

Serialize `Filter` as the specification declares it: `vms`, `names`, `folders`, `datacenters`, `hosts`, `clusters`, `resource_pools`, `power_states`, each `style: form`, `explode: true`, `uniqueItems: true`. Emit the set members in that declared order regardless of the order the caller populated them, repeat a member's key once per value with the values in caller order and each value query escaped, and keep a member's repeated keys contiguous. Omit every unset member: a nil slice and an empty slice are alike absent, never a blank value, an empty key, or a bare query delimiter, and a wholly unset filter produces a target with no `?` at all. Reject a filter member holding a blank or repeated value before sending anything.

Require each `Vcenter.VM_list` success to be exactly HTTP 200 with JSON media type and a non-null JSON array of `Vcenter.VM.Summary` objects. The specification-required `vm`, `name`, and `power_state` must be nonblank strings and `vm` must be unique. The optional `cpu_count` and `memory_size_mib` must be non-boolean integers when present; preserve their absence or null as a nil `VM.CPUCount` or `VM.MemorySizeMiB`. Return the summaries in response order, and return no partial slice on failure.

Run `go test -race ./...`. The protected table-driven verifier starts the shipped contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port and reads its synchronized in-process request log, which records arrival order, completion order, and whether a response was produced on a session that had already been deleted. The mock loads its only three callable routes from `docs/contract.json`. Verification holds one `Vcenter.VM_list` request open across a rotation and asserts the exact request sequence, raw targets, header multiplicity and absence, bodylessness, the token carried by each request, that the replacement session existed before the previous one was retired, that the previous session was deleted only after the request still using it had completed, and that every unset optional filter member was omitted rather than sent. The verifier never contacts a live VMware endpoint.
scenario: A Vcenter.VM_list request is held open on the current session token while the service credential rotates, so Cis.Session_create for the replacement secret must precede retirement of the previous token and Cis.Session_delete must wait for the request still using it.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact bodyless wire shape of all three operations, including complete omission of every unset optional filter member rather than an empty or default representation, and its completion ordering proves no request was answered on an already-deleted session.
